$comment: Everything Jev reads is in here, the tier describe text, redo_cost, risk and the skills. Tune the wording here not the scripts

policy.$provider_preference: codex | claude | balanced. codex = send anything codex-suitable to codex to save Claude quota. balanced = alternate by tier: T0/T1 codex, T2/T3 claude.

tiers.name: trivial
tiers.describe: Trivial mechanical work: rename a symbol, fix a typo, add a docstring, format code, write a commit message, look up where something is defined, list files, apply an obvious one-line fix with no judgment needed.

tiers.name: routine
tiers.describe: Routine engineering work with a clear spec: write unit tests for an existing function, implement a small well-defined feature in one or two files, fix a bug whose cause is already known, do a review pass for style and obvious errors, update docs to match code.

tiers.name: hard
tiers.describe: Hard work needing investigation and judgment: multi-file refactor, debugging a failure whose cause is unknown, integrating two subsystems, performance work with measurement, a feature that touches data models and their consumers.

tiers.name: frontier
tiers.describe: Frontier work: architecture and system design, security-sensitive changes such as auth or crypto or input handling at trust boundaries, novel algorithms, ambiguous or conflicting requirements that need interpretation, anything where a wrong answer is expensive and hard to detect.

redo_cost: Cheap: result is easy to check at a glance and trivial to redo, such as a rename, a doc edit, a lookup, or a formatting change.
Moderate: checking needs running tests or reading a diff; redoing costs a few minutes.
Expensive: a wrong result is hard to detect or costly to unwind, such as data migrations, security logic, public API shape, or anything already depended on by other subtasks.
risk: Safe and reversible: edits inside the working tree, new files, reads, test runs.
Moderate: touches config, dependencies, build scripts, CI, or shared interfaces; reversible with effort.
Destructive or irreversible: deletes data or branches, force-pushes, rewrites history, changes production config or secrets, runs migrations against real data, sends anything external.

skills.none: No listed skill fits; the worker should proceed with plain coding-agent behavior.
skills.codex-quick: Mechanical edits and lookups done by a cheap Codex model: renames, typos, docstrings, formatting, simple one-line fixes, listing or locating code.
skills.codex-standard: Routine implementation by a mid Codex model: unit tests, small features, known-cause bug fixes, doc sync, straightforward refactors within a couple of files.
skills.codex-deep: Hard or frontier implementation by the top Codex model at high reasoning: multi-file refactors, unknown-cause debugging, integration, design-heavy features.
skills.codex-review: Read-only code review by Codex of a diff, branch, or file set; returns findings, does not edit.
skills.codex-research: Read-only investigation by Codex: map a codebase area, trace a call path, summarize how something works, compare options; returns findings JSON, does not edit.
